title: Change and continuity table
subject: History
unit: Spring 1: The history of sports tournaments (Mighty Metals)
source: Seeded from history/y3 lesson 8 (Change and continuity table (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 8: Modern tournaments: the Olympics, Paralympics and World Cup. To understand how modern tournaments began and how they compare with older ones

questions.q: Name one thing that has stayed the same since ancient times.
questions.a: For example: held every four years, or running races

questions.q: Core: Fill in a change and continuity table comparing the ancient and modern Olympics (3 changes, 2 continuities).
questions.a: Changes: medals not wreaths; women compete; athletes from all countries. Continuities: every four years; running races
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: 'Change: ancient winners got wreaths, now they get medals.'

questions.q: Extend: Add the Paralympics to your tournaments timeline.
questions.a: 1948 Stoke Mandeville games; 1960 first Paralympics in Rome

questions.q: Stretch: Why was starting the Paralympics an important change?
questions.a: It gave disabled athletes the chance to compete and be respected

questions.q: The first modern Olympics were in:
Big question: what has changed in tournaments since ancient times, and what has stayed the same?
questions.a: Changed: prizes, who can compete, many countries. Same: every four years, races, fame for winners
